notes: Baked 2026-11-16 with Blender 5.2 Mantaflow liquid (FLIP), headless; scripts in bake_other_side_20261116/scripts (splash_sim.py, splash_dump.py, splash_process.py, splash_pack.mjs). Each GLB: 40 meshes/nodes frame_000..frame_039 in time order, identity node transforms, no materials. POSITION float32 (snapped to 1/4096), NORMAL int8 normalized (smooth, area-weighted), uint16 indices, <=15000 triangles per frame (meshoptimizer simplify from ~250-450k). Compression: EXT_meshopt_compression (+KHR_mesh_quantization for the int8 normals) - needs GLTFLoader.setMeshoptDecoder(MeshoptDecoder), verified with three r170's stock loader in Node. Space: y up, still water y=0, impact at origin. The surface was cut 6 mm above the still water level and shifted down so the open cut edge lies exactly on y=0 (min y = 0); low pool-surface patches beyond 1.6 radii are removed, flying droplets are kept out to 3 radii. outerRadius=1.0 is the crown rim radius (90th percentile radius of the wall) at peakFrame = the frame where the crown wall is tallest. AFTER the peak the rim keeps flaring outward to ~1.6-1.7 (see rimRadiusPerFrame), and droplets fly to ~1.9. Frame 0-1 contain the falling drop above the water (hence a high maxY there). splash_a ends with the central rebound jet rising (maxHeight is that jet; crownHeightAtPeak is the crown). splash_b ends with the ring collapsed. fps=24 is the intended slow-motion playback (1.67 s); the 40 frames span ~0.39 s of simulated time at metre scale, sim frames are near-uniform (see simFrames). Topology changes every frame: swap meshes, do not morph. Extra fields beyond the contract: crownHeightAtPeak, rimRadiusPerFrame, maxYPerFrame, trisPerFrame, simFrames, metresPerUnit, bytes, sim.
